todos.title: Cost model: is the 5-25bp equity constant invalidating KILLs?
todos.detail: Measured US equity round-trip cost = 0.9756bp (CS spread 0.7696 + SEC 0.206; zero commission/ECN, FX avoided; 191 names, 356,271 1-min bars). Repo charges 5.0bp or 25.0bp -> 5-25x too high. Built tools/cost_sensitivity.py to separate SIGN flips from VERDICT flips. HML worked through: breakeven cost 6.16bp sits inside [0.98,25] so the SIGN flips, but at the cheapest cost HML nets +0.09%/yr vs a 4.32% hurdle -> verdict does NOT flip. Assessment ROBUSTLY-KILLED. Conclusion: hurdle-based KILLs are robust to the cost model; sign-based judgements are not. Recommended rule: require breakeven_cost_bp > cost_high_bp. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: components recompose to 0.975600bp exactly, and recomputing median(cs_bp) over the 65 usable symbols from per_symbol gives 0.769640 + SEC 0.206 = 0.9756bp, matching the stored total. Ratios: 5.0bp constant is 5.13x the measurement, 25.0bp is 25.63x. FINAL MEASURED ROUND-TRIP = 0.9756 bp.
